title: Decision-making roles
label: 04-Decision Makers
markdown:
# Decision-making roles

## Image 1: Operators - Boss/General Manager/COO

| Classification of information | Specific content |
| --- | --- |
| Typical background | Founder, general manager or manager of the enterprise; |
| Typical background | Most of these are growth-oriented enterprises that have created the complexities of cross-sectoral collaboration; |
| Typical background | There is interest in the concept of technology but value is judged by profit, cash flow, turnover and speed of implementation. |
| Core tasks (JTBD) | ** As the size of the enterprise expands and the sector increases, I want to know the true state of sales, procurement, inventory, delivery and refunds at all times and to allow decision-making to land quickly, rather than waiting for manual aggregation. ** |
| It hurts. | Each department has its own form and calibre; |
| It hurts. | Business reports are lagging behind and cannot be followed up; |
| It hurts. | Multiple systems have been purchased, but data are still not available; |
| It hurts. | Mid-level management relies on experience and processes are difficult to monitor; |
| It hurts. | Interested in AI but not knowing how to make a profit. |
| Purchase trigger | Rapid expansion, opening of new areas or mergers and acquisitions; |
| Purchase trigger | Loss of stock, loss of customers, delay in refunding; |
| Purchase trigger | The cost of upgrading the original system is too high; |
| Purchase trigger | Board/management requests for AI or digitization. |
| Key purchasing drivers | A cockpit to see the operation; |
| Key purchasing drivers | Reducing the cost of software and manpower with a platform; |
| Key purchasing drivers | Quantifiable results are seen in 1-3 months; |
| Key purchasing drivers | The system can be adapted to business changes. |
| Main resistance | It is feared that another set of “fill-up tools” will be purchased. |
| Main resistance | Concerns about long project time and staff conflicts; |
| Main resistance | Doubts about the stability of young brands and service capacity; |
| Main resistance | It is difficult to verify efficiency figures in marketing calibres. |

## Image 2: Head of Growth - Director of Sales/Director of Operations

| Classification of information | Specific content |
| --- | --- |
| Typical background | Management of the 10-100-person sales team; |
| Typical background | (a) High per capita prices, long sales cycles, channels and direct sales; |
| Typical background | There is a need to explain to the boss the accuracy of forecasts and team execution. |
| Core tasks (JTBD) | ** I want the customer's assets to be deposited in the company, to know what each business is going to do next, and to identify the risk of loss and return in advance. ** |
| It hurts. | Client information in mainstream social tools, mobile phones and personal forms; |
| It hurts. | Sales are reluctant to enter CRM; |
| It hurts. | The follow-up process is not transparent and the client is removed from service; |
| It hurts. | (a) The price, contract, order, refund and after sale; |
| It hurts. | Management statements are time-consuming and not credible. |
| Purchase trigger | (a) Increase in the number of clues but decrease in conversion rates; |
| Purchase trigger | Large clients lost or sold out; |
| Purchase trigger | Need for standardized sales SOP; |
| Purchase trigger | The boss wants more accurate performance projections. |
| Key purchasing drivers | AI Automatic filing, reminder, summary and analysis to reduce sales entry; |
| Key purchasing drivers | From clue to refund/sale; |
| Key purchasing drivers | Self-defined niche marketing processes; |
| Key purchasing drivers | As management can see, sales still feel good. |
| Main resistance | Concerned that the system will add a first-line burden; |
| Main resistance | Ignorance of integration with mainstream business office platforms, telephones, mail and former ERP; |
| Main resistance | AI recommended accuracy and disclosure of customer information; |
| Main resistance | Team usage and data quality are difficult to ensure. |

## Image 3: Deduction gatekeeper - procurement/supply chain/storage People

| Classification of information | Specific content |
| --- | --- |
| Typical background | Manufacturing, trade, energy, renewable resources, retail or equipment services; |
| Typical background | Management of vendors, multiple warehouses, multiple SKU, treasury, quality checks and reconciliations. |
| Core tasks (JTBD) | ** I would like to make faster and more retroactive decisions between prices, quality, delivery and stocks to reduce stock shortages, backlogs, mispayments and larceny. ** |
| It hurts. | (b) Time-consuming request-for-price and subjective evaluation by suppliers; |
| It hurts. | Procurement, warehouse, quality control and financial documentation cannot be automatically matched; |
| It hurts. | The inventory did not match; |
| It hurts. | Price volatility and reliance on safe stocks; |
| It hurts. | Retroactive materials for compliance are difficult to generate. |
| Purchase trigger | Increased prices of raw materials, loss of stock or audit issues; |
| Purchase trigger | Multiple silo expansion or rapid growth of SKU; |
| Purchase trigger | Customer demand for supply chain traceability; |
| Purchase trigger | Financial integration is required. |
| Key purchasing drivers | Procurement-entry-quality-reconciling-payment closure; |
| Key purchasing drivers | AI Adjudication, stock alert and supplier assessment; |
| Key purchasing drivers | Bar code/sweep and move-end operations; |
| Key purchasing drivers | Data can be traced and supported by management questions. |
| Key purchasing drivers | The Kuailu procurement page is clearly geared towards procurement, warehouse and financial synergies and describes processes such as AI value-for-money, automatic purchase orders generation, warehousing and write-off of payments. [Source: Kuailu Procurement Management] (https://www.kuailutech.cn/biz/proc) |
| Main resistance | (b) The cost of cleaning basic materials and supplier data; |
| Main resistance | AI Auxiliary price coverage, price prescription and liability boundaries; |
| Main resistance | Duplication with existing ERP/financial systems; |
| Main resistance | Storage site network, equipment and operating habits. |

## Image 4: Technical Portrait - Head of IT/Information

| Classification of information | Specific content |
| --- | --- |
| Typical background | Responsible for system selection, integration, authority, security and management of peacekeeping vendors; |
| Typical background | Often it is not a budget sponsor, but it may have a de facto veto. |
| Core tasks (JTBD) | ** Without undermining the stability of the existing system, I will introduce governance AI and visualization configuration capabilities and ensure data, privileges and traffic control. ** |
| It hurts. | (a) The operational units continue to submit ad hoc requests; |
| It hurts. | Multiple systems interfaces are complex and lead data are inconsistent; |
| It hurts. | (a) The loss of control of visual configuration applications may create a new shadow IT; |
| It hurts. | AI Model calls, data flows and unclear audit responsibilities; |
| It hurts. | There are many commitments from suppliers and insufficient technical files and SLA. |
| Purchase trigger | The boss wants to land fast AI; |
| Purchase trigger | The cost of the two-tier system is too high; |
| Purchase trigger | (b) Safety restructuring or nationalization requirements; |
| Purchase trigger | There is a need for integrated application of building and governance. |
| Key purchasing drivers | API, database connector and SSO; |
| Key purchasing drivers | Privatization/mixed deployment; |
| Key purchasing drivers | fine particle size privileges, logs, backup, recovery and data export; |
| Key purchasing drivers | Visible configuration development specifications, version control and application governance; |
| Key purchasing drivers | Clear models, knowledge base and data boundaries. |
| Main resistance | Lack of structure and evaluation material for expressions such as “self-study larger models”; |
| Main resistance | Lack of clarity on the boundaries of responsibilities with existing ERP/CRM/OA; |
| Main resistance | Size of suppliers, delivery capacity and long-term operating risks; |
| Main resistance | Costs of hardware, upgrade and maintenance deployed under privatization. |
